description: Gate hygiene (GX-19, D-070): the per-stage time limit and the retention of report directories and build-cache entries.

gate-gc.build_cache_keep.description: Build-cache entries kept per build target (production, test); the most recently used win and older ones are removed when a gate exits.

gate-gc.kill_grace_s.description: Seconds between the TERM and the KILL sent to a stage that ran past its limit.

gate-gc.log_tail_lines.description: Lines of a timed-out stage's log printed with its failure.

gate-gc.proc_dir.description: The process table the folder bound reads to learn which sha directories a live process holds (an open descriptor or a working directory under one); where it does not exist, nothing is known to be held and only the calling gate's own sha and a held gate lock protect.

gate-gc.report_only_shas_keep.description: Sha directories kept under the report-only (advisory) record directory's reports: the same folder bound as gate-gc.reports_shas_keep for the head tooling's advisory runs, whose verdict is already posted on the PR. Set from the readers' need: one train batch (train.batch_size).
gate-gc.report_only_shas_keep.x-source: D-070, D-069 item 4; GATE-GC-CHEIO audit step 3; review by 2026-11-28

gate-gc.reports_keep.description: Report directories kept per (sha, mode) under the gate record directory; the newest win and older ones are removed when a gate exits.

gate-gc.reports_shas_keep.description: Sha directories kept under the gate record directory's reports (the folder bound, beside the per-(sha, mode) gate-gc.reports_keep): every push adds a sha, so without it the folder grows without ceiling. The most recent win; a sha a live gate writes or a live process holds is never removed. Set from the readers' need: two train batches (train.batch_size x train.queue_growing_batches), never below gate.status_history_runs.
gate-gc.reports_shas_keep.x-source: D-070, D-069 item 4; GATE-GC-CHEIO audit step 3; review by 2026-11-28

gate-gc.stage_timeout_s.description: Wall-clock limit of one gate stage, by stage name; the entry named * applies to every stage not listed, and every other entry names a stage the gate runs (gate_policy.FULL_STAGES). A stage that overruns is killed and ends red with class env and its log tail. Set above the field p99 of the stage, never shorter (GA-PG5): raising an entry is the rollback.

gate-gc.timeout_exit_code.description: Exit status the gate records for a stage that ran past its limit (the status timeout(1) uses).
